elements.name: Opening
elements.html:
Protocol: SRSD384-101

Sponsor: Sirius Therapeutics

Phase: 1/2a

 

Opening 

 

Thank you for your interest in our weight loss clinical trial. As you may or may not know, obesity is rapidly increasing as a worldwide concern due to its innate risk factor for other life-threatening conditions such as type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease or heart failure. As such, there is an ongoing and urgent need to achieve sustained weight loss.

 

Therefore, this phase 1/2a study will be assessing the safety and effectiveness of a new medication to support weight loss.

elements.name: Study Drug and Design
elements.html:
Study Drug and Design

 

The investigational product for this study is called SRSD384. Compared to other treatments for weight loss such as Ozempic which works by suppressing hunger, SRSD384 works by preventing cells in the liver from producing a chemical called Activin E. This production prevention helps break down fat stores in the body.

 

The study drug will be administered through subcutaneous injection (injection just below the skin). This study involves a combination therapy, meaning along with the study drug, you will receive weekly doses of Tirzepatide.

 

Tirzepatide is also known by as its brand names, Mounjaro and Zepbound. This is one of the earlier mentioned drugs that can suppress hunger.

 

You will be split into 1 of 3 groups:

 

Group 1: 100mg SRSD384 (low dose)

Group 2: 300mg SRSD384 (moderate dose)

Group 3: 600mg SRSD384 (higher dose)

 

Within each group, you have a 77% chance of receiving the study drug, and a 23% chance of receiving a placebo.

 

Everyone in the study will also be on Tirzepatide, including the participants on the placebo. You'll receive, as subcutaneous injections, 2.5mg once a week for the first 4 weeks. After that, you'll receive 5mg once a week for 20 weeks. 

 

As this study is double-blinded, neither you nor the doctors will know which group you’re in until the end of the trial.

elements.name: Study Duration and Scheduling
elements.html:
Study Duration and Scheduling


Total participation time in this study is expected to last up to 28 weeks, or just about 6 and a half months, with 14 visits to the clinic.

 

The first few weeks require frequent visits. After this the visits become more spread out.

 

The screening period involves an initial screening visit, returning for bloods in the morning another day, and getting an MRI in a separate location. 

If you are found to be eligible, the beginning of the study requires 3 visits in 3 consecutive days. The first day's visit will be long (approximately 8-10 hours).

 

After this, follow-up visits are shorter, taking around 2 hours each, and are less frequent.


After the screening, the visits are as follows:

  • 3 visits in the first 3 days (D0-D2) as mentioned
  • Follow-up visits at the end of week 1 and 2
  • Follow-up visits every 2 weeks from week 2-16
  • Follow-up visits every 4 weeks from week 16-24

 

Follow-up visits include checking body composition, and blood tests, and some will include MRIs as well. Some of these will also be fasting visits. The study doctors can specify which visits entail which tests, and assuming we can book you in, I will also send you a document outlining the visits.

 

These MRI scans will be conducted at a separate location on 20-22 Mons Rd, Westmead NSW 2145

 

You will be taught how to administer the Tirzepatide injection yourself, so that you don't have to come in every week.

elements.name: Reimbursement
elements.html:
Reimbursement

 

You will be reimbursed the following amounts for any reasonable travel, parking, meals and other expenses associated with your study visits. 

 

  • $350 per clinic visit 
  • $150 for imaging clinic visit
  • $150 for return for fasting bloods

 

This means if you attend all scheduled visits, you can receive up to $5000.

 

You may also receive up to $350 for any unscheduled visits the study team may deem necessary. These are not included in the total I just mentioned.

 

The study team will let you know if you're eligible for extra reimbursement related to rural travel.

elements.name: Disclosure
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before you even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.name: BW Stable
elements.title: Has your body weight been stable for the past 3 months?
elements.description: Stable is defined as no change greater than +/- 5%. If greater than 5%, please exclude.

elements.name: BW Stable Info
elements.html:
Example for the 5% rule:

 

Starting weight: 70 kg

  • 5% weight change = 3.5 kg

     

    • More than 5% weight change (not allowed):
      • Weight loss of 4 kg → New weight: 66 kg (5.71% loss)

      • Weight gain of 4.5 kg → New weight: 74.5 kg (6.43% gain)

         

    • Less than 5% weight change (allowed):
      • Weight loss of 2.5 kg → New weight: 67.5 kg (3.57% loss)

      • Weight gain of 2 kg → New weight: 72 kg (2.86% gain)

         

For this example, changes greater than 3.5 kg (either loss or gain) are not allowed, while changes less than 3.5 kg are acceptable.

Please keep in mind that these values change according to the starting weight! For example, for a person who weighs 120kg, a 5% weight change would be 6kg.

elements.name: question11
elements.html:
Please use the following formula to calculate bodyweight stability in the past 3 months

 

Highest body weight - Lowest body weight / Highest body weight = n

 

n x 100 = percentage of weight loss in the past 3 months

 

The percentage of weight loss in the past 3 months needs to be 5% or under.

Stage C - Symptomatic Heart Failure

  • People with current or previous symptoms of heart failure

 

Stage D - Advanced heart failure

  • People with heart failure symptoms that disrupt daily life functions or lead to being hospitalised

 

Heart failure symptoms include:

  • Persistent shortness of breath (especially when lying flat or during activity)
  • Extreme fatigue
  • Sudden unexplained weight gain
  • Swelling in the legs, ankles, or abdomen

elements.name: Exclusionary Medical History Info
elements.html:
PLEASE EXCLUDE THE FOLLOWING

  • Unstable body weight within the past 3 months
  • Any form of non-type 2 diabetes 
  • Obesity due to medications, endocrinologic or genetic disorders
  • History of thyroid C-cell tumours, multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome type 2, thyroid dysfunction, or thyroid hormone abnormality
  • History of an endoscopic or surgical treatment for weight loss
  • History of a device-based therapy for weight loss
  • Intolerance to GLP-1 RA
  • Intolerance to antisense oligonucleotides/small interfering RNA drugs
  • Tattoos or skin conditions that could interfere with study assessments or obscure observation of potential reactions
  • Cancer within the past 2 years
  • Major surgery within the past 90 days, or planned surgery during the study
  • History of syphilis, HIV with a low T-helper cell count, or active Hep B or C
  • History of drug or alcohol abuse
  • History of major depressive disorder 
  • Donation of blood, plasma or blood products in the past 30 days
  • History of heart failure
  • History of heart conditions in the last 3 months
  • History of pancreatitis

elements.name: Booking Cancellation
elements.title: Please note that by booking in your appointment this does not guarantee your participation in the trial. Clinical trials can experience delays or cancellations due to various factors. We will aim to notify you 24 to 48 hours before your appointment if we need to cancel or reschedule, however there are chances of same day cancellations. Is this okay?

elements.name: Referral Intro
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: Referral Details
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
